newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea garment maker New Star hit by takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea garment maker New Star hit by takeover bid.

text.p: South Korean garment maker New Star Trading Co on Wednesday said it would fight to thwart a hostile takeover bid by a Seoul-based hotel.
The Korea Stock Exchange said Savoy Hotel had bought 11.11 percent of New Star's outstanding shares in the open market on April 9-10, raising its stake in New Star to 24.7 percent.
It exceeded the 23.17 percent stake held by the family of New Star's chairman, according to an exchange statement.
"We see Savoy's recent purchase of an additional stake in our company as a takeover bid," Kim Hong-gil, an executive director of New Star, told Reuters.
"When taking into account the stake held by those friendly to us, the actual stake supporting our current owner stands at around 40 percent," he said by telephone, without elaborating.
If Savoy's move succeeded, it would be the nation's first hostile takeover of a listed company, but analysts said Savoy seemed to be more interested in making money than in expanding.
"I don't think Savoy really wants to expand into the garment making business," said a Hyundai Securities analyst. "This is seen as a sort of 'greenmailing'."
He was referring to a practice of accumulating a company's shares and later asking the existing owner to buy the shares at a much higher price than the stock's market price.
Savoy officials confirmed the purchase, but declined to give details.
New Star unveiled a symbolic 1-for-100 bonus issue plan on May 2, aimed at raising the existing owner's stake and giving a chance to analyse the shareholding structure.
Under the securities regulations, holders of fewer than 100 shares will be given cash instead of new shares, and the company will receive the bonus shares of these small shareholders.

The news sent New Star's shares skyrocketing as investors expected one or both of the two sides to offer tenders to buy more shares to win the game, although none of the two companies has yet disclosed a tender offer plan.
New Star shares closed Wednesday's session 4,200 won higher at a record high of 57,100 won ($63.80) per share. This was triple the stock's lowest close of 18,700 won for this year.
Under the revised securities regulations that went into force on April 1, investors are now able to buy up to 25 percent of a listed company's oustanding shares.
If an investor, or a group of investors, want to hold 25 percent or more of a firm's shares, they must buy shares through tender offers until their stake exceeds 50 percent.
A recent bid by Shindongbang Corp to take over Midopa Department Store Co had fizzled out after a third large shareholder turned against Shindongbang.
Instead the Sungwon Group, once regarded as a partner of Shindongbang, sold all its holding of Midopa shares to Midopa's owner Dainong Corp at a price far higher than the stock's market price.
